verses.english: Numbered Discourses 7.64
6. The Undeclared Points
Irritable

verses.pali: “Sattime, bhikkhave, dhammā sapattakantā sapattakaraṇā kodhanaṁ āgacchanti itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these seven things that please and assist an enemy happen to an irritable woman or man.
What seven?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Firstly, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only they’d become ugly!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa vaṇṇavatāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have a beautiful enemy.

verses.pali: Kodhanoyaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo kodhābhibhūto kodhapareto, kiñcāpi so hoti sunhāto suvilitto kappitakesamassu odātavatthavasano;
verses.english: An irritable individual, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, is ugly, even though they’re nicely bathed and anointed, with hair and beard dressed, and wearing white clothes.

verses.pali: atha kho so dubbaṇṇova hoti kodhābhibhūto.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the first thing that pleases and assists an enemy which happens to an irritable woman or man.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only they’d sleep badly!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa sukhaseyyāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have an enemy who sleeps at ease.

verses.pali: Kodhanoyaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo kodhābhibhūto kodhapareto, kiñcāpi so pallaṅke seti gonakatthate paṭalikatthate kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇe sauttaracchade ubhatolohitakūpadhāne;
verses.english: An irritable individual, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, sleeps badly, even though they sleep on a couch spread with woolen covers—shag-piled, pure white, or embroidered with flowers—and spread with a fine deer hide, with a canopy above and red pillows at both ends.

verses.pali: atha kho so dukkhaññeva seti kodhābhibhūto.
Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the second thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only their needs are not amply satisfied!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa pacuratthatāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have an enemy whose needs are amply satisfied.

verses.pali: Kodhanoyaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo kodhābhibhūto kodhapareto, anatthampi gahetvā ‘attho me gahito’ti maññati, atthampi gahetvā ‘anattho me gahito’ti maññati.
verses.english: When an irritable individual, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, gets what they don’t need they think, ‘I’ve got what I need.’ When they get what they need they think, ‘I’ve got what I don’t need.’

verses.pali: Tassime dhammā aññamaññaṁ vipaccanīkā gahitā dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti kodhābhibhūtassa.
verses.english: When an angry person gets these things that are the exact opposite of what they need, it’s for their lasting harm and suffering.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the third thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only they weren’t wealthy!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa bhogavatāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have an enemy who is wealthy.

verses.pali: Kodhanassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa kodhābhibhūtassa kodhaparetassa, yepissa te honti bhogā uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatā bāhābalaparicitā sedāvakkhittā dhammikā dhammaladdhā, tepi rājāno rājakosaṁ pavesenti kodhābhibhūtassa.
verses.english: When an individual is irritable, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, the rulers seize the legitimate wealth they’ve earned by their efforts, built up with their own hands, gathered by the sweat of their brow.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the fourth thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only they weren’t famous!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa yasavatāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have a famous enemy.

verses.pali: Kodhanoyaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo kodhābhibhūto kodhapareto, yopissa so hoti yaso appamādādhigato, tamhāpi dhaṁsati kodhābhibhūto.
verses.english: When an individual is irritable, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, any fame they have acquired by diligence falls to dust.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the fifth thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:
‘If only they had no friends!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa mittavatāya nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have an enemy with friends.

verses.pali: Kodhanaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalaṁ kodhābhibhūtaṁ kodhaparetaṁ, yepissa te honti mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā, tepi ārakā parivajjanti kodhābhibhūtaṁ.
verses.english: When an individual is irritable, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, their friends and colleagues, relatives and kin avoid them from afar.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, chaṭṭho dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the sixth thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa evaṁ icchati:
verses.english: Furthermore, an enemy wishes for an enemy:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāyaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell!’
Why is that?

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, sapatto sapattassa sugatigamane nandati.
verses.english: Because an enemy doesn’t like to have an enemy who goes to a good place.

verses.pali: Kodhanoyaṁ, bhikkhave, purisapuggalo kodhābhibhūto kodhapareto kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
verses.english: When an individual is irritable, overcome and overwhelmed by anger, they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati kodhābhibhūto.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, sattamo dhammo sapattakanto sapattakaraṇo kodhanaṁ āgacchati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā.
verses.english: This is the seventh thing that pleases and assists an enemy which happens to an irritable woman or man.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta dhammā sapattakantā sapattakaraṇā kodhanaṁ āgacchanti itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vāti.
verses.english: These are the seven things that please and assist an enemy which happen to an irritable woman or man.
An irritable person is ugly
and they sleep badly.
When they get what they need,
they take it to be what they don’t need.
An angry person
kills with body or speech;
overcome with anger,
they lose their wealth.
Mad with anger,
they fall into disgrace.
Family, friends, and loved ones
avoid an irritable person.
Anger creates harm;
anger upsets the mind.
That person doesn’t recognize
the danger that arises within.
An angry person doesn’t know the good.
An angry person doesn’t see the truth.
When a person is beset by anger,
only blind darkness is left.
An angry person destroys with ease
what was hard to build.
Afterwards, when the anger is spent,
they’re tormented as if burnt by fire.
Their look betrays their sulkiness
like a fire’s smoky plume.
And when their anger flares up,
they make others angry.
They have no conscience or prudence,
nor any respectful speech.
One overcome by anger
has no island refuge anywhere.
The deeds that torment a man
are far from those that are good.
I’ll explain them now;
listen to this, for it is the truth.
An angry person slays their father;
their mother, too, they slay.
An angry person slays a saint;
a normal person, too, they slay.
A man is raised by his mother,
who shows him the world.
But an angry ordinary person slays
even that good woman who gave him life.
Like oneself, those sentient beings
hold themselves most dear.
But when angered, they kill themselves in different ways,
distraught in many respects.
Some kill themselves with swords,
some, distraught, take poison.
Some hang themselves with rope,
or fling themselves down a mountain gorge.
When they commit deeds of killing babes
and killing themselves,
they don’t realize what they do,
for anger leads to their downfall.
The snare of death in the form of anger
lies hidden in the heart.
You should cut it out by self-control,
by wisdom, energy, and right ideas.
An astute person should cut out
this unskillful thing.
And they’d train in the teaching in just the same way,
not yielding to sulkiness.
Free of anger, free of despair,
free of greed, with no more longing,
tamed, having given up anger,
the undefiled are fully extinguished.
